problem: What is ${\int }_{2}^{6}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{j}=a+jΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{2}^{6}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ the lower bound is $a=2$ and the upper bound is $b=6.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{6-2}{n}=\frac{4}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{6}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}[f(2+j\cdot \frac{4}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}[f(2+\frac{4j}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}[\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2+\frac{4j}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
